findings.summary: Attempt-1 coverage gap (ComputeEffectiveScale safe-area clamp branch and resolver tolerant-undefined fallback) remains closed by two non-vacuous tests.
findings.detail: BadgeSizePositionTests.SafeAreaClampReducesTheEffectiveScaleOnAShortPoster is a 3-case theory (Medium 3000x120, Large 1000x40, Small 1000x30). In each case the unclamped ComputeScale * SizeFactor exceeds min(width,height)/(2*OuterInset), so the clamp at BadgeGeometry.cs binds; the test asserts unclamped > expected and effective == min(width,height)/48, so removing or weakening the clamp would fail it. RendererConfigurationTests.ResolverFallsBackToDefaultsForUndefinedBadgePositionAndSize passes (BadgePosition)99/(BadgeSize)99 through RendererConfigurationResolver.ResolveOutputPolicy and asserts the code-owned defaults (BottomLeft/Medium) plus a defined TopRight/Large case, so a regression that propagated the undefined value would fail it. Both are deterministic and assert concrete values. Production and test files are unchanged since the attempt-2 review.

findings.summary: The clamp wording says the safe area 'stays positive' although at the clamp boundary it is exactly zero (non-negative).
findings.detail: BadgeGeometry.ComputeEffectiveScale and the changelog say the scaled inset 'leaves a positive safe area'; at scale == maximumInsetScale the safe area in the minimum dimension is exactly zero. The invariant that matters (no badge paints outside the safe area) still holds, and the added clamp test asserts >= -0.000001. This wording is pre-existing attempt-1 production code, unchanged by attempt 3, and is not a canonical current-state surface. No action required.
